subject.title: Hard-delete or runtimeId migration needed for @apify/apify-openclaw-plugin

question: Should an authorized ClawHub operator apply the guarded runtime-ID repair to the production Apify package after verifying publisher authority and target-ID collision state?
rationale: The production mismatch is confirmed and the repair mechanism is already deployed, but automation cannot authorize a production mutation that changes executable plugin identity.

options.title: Apply guarded repair
options.body: Run the existing dry-run and then apply the runtime-ID repair after verifying Apify control and no active target-ID collision.

options.title: Keep package blocked
options.body: Leave the record unchanged until stronger publisher-authority or collision evidence is available.

options.title: Retire or delete record
options.body: Use a destructive package retirement path only if the identity-preserving repair cannot safely produce the intended state.

recommendation.title: Apply guarded repair
recommendation.body: Run the existing dry-run and then apply the runtime-ID repair after verifying Apify control and no active target-ID collision.

likelyOwner.reason: They implemented the runtime-ID-specific operator flow and the analogous production package repair.
